#!/bin/sh
#flux: --job-name=runDisplacmentCalculation-<TMPL_VAR NAME=iJob>
#flux: --account=<TMPL_VAR NAME=linuxUser>
#flux: --mail-user=<TMPL_VAR NAME=emailAddress>
#flux: --mail-type=ABORT
#flux: --time=20:00:00
#flux: --nodes=1
#flux: --ntasks=1
#flux: --mem-per-node=1300M
#flux: --output=<TMPL_VAR NAME=outDir>/out.displacmentCalculation-<TMPL_VAR NAME=conditionSetTimeStamp>-<TMPL_VAR NAME=iJob>.log
#flux: --error=<TMPL_VAR NAME=outDir>/err.displacmentCalculation-<TMPL_VAR NAME=conditionSetTimeStamp>-<TMPL_VAR NAME=iJob>.log
# The PBS user/group directive '-P' was translated to the Flux '--account' directive.
# The PBS mail trigger '-m a' (on abort) has been translated to '--mail-type=ABORT'.
# The PBS virtual memory request '-l vmem=5gb' has been omitted as there is no direct
# equivalent in Flux. The physical memory request ('-l mem=1300mb') has been preserved.
# Performance implication: If the application's virtual memory usage exceeds system limits
# based on the physical memory allocation, it may be terminated.
# The PBS umask directive '-W umask=002' has no direct Flux equivalent and was omitted.

#set environment
export MATLAB_PREFDIR=/tmp/emptydir

# The PBS_JOBID variable has been replaced with the Flux equivalent, FLUX_JOB_ID.
export MCR_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/mcr_cache_$FLUX_JOB_ID
export XAPPLRESDIR=/usr/local/bin/MATLAB/MATLAB_Compiler_Runtime/v716/X11/app-defaults
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:/usr/local/bin/MATLAB/MATLAB_Compiler_Runtime/v716/runtime/glnxa64:/usr/local/bin/MATLAB/MATLAB_Compiler_Runtime/v716/sys/os/glnxa64:/usr/local/bin/MATLAB/MATLAB_Compiler_Runtime/v716/sys/java/jre/glnxa64/jre/lib/amd64/native_threads:/usr/local/bin/MATLAB/MATLAB_Compiler_Runtime/v716/sys/java/jre/glnxa64/jre/lib/amd64/server:/usr/local/bin/MATLAB/MATLAB_Compiler_Runtime/v716/sys/java/jre/glnxa64/jre/lib/amd64
mkdir -p $MCR_CACHE_ROOT

#setup
cd <TMPL_VAR NAME=baseDir>

#job
./run.sh runDisplacementCalculation \
  <TMPL_VAR NAME=pathToRunTime> \
  <TMPL_VAR NAME=outDir>/matlab.displacmentCalculation.<TMPL_VAR NAME=conditionSetTimeStamp>.<TMPL_VAR NAME=iJob>.log \
  <TMPL_VAR NAME=conditionSetTimeStamp> <TMPL_VAR NAME=iJob> <TMPL_VAR NAME=outDir>

#cleanup
rm -rf $MCR_CACHE_ROOT/*

#resources
echo ""
echo "=============="
echo "=== status ==="
echo "=============="
# The 'qstat' command has been replaced with 'flux job info' to check job status.
flux job info $FLUX_JOB_ID

#status
if [[ -f "<TMPL_VAR NAME=outDir>/err.displacmentCalculation-<TMPL_VAR NAME=conditionSetTimeStamp>-<TMPL_VAR NAME=iJob>.log" ]]
then
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

reasons: The script uses placeholders like '<TMPL_VAR NAME=iJob>', '<TMPL_VAR NAME=linuxUser>', '<TMPL_VAR NAME=emailAddress>', '<TMPL_VAR NAME=outDir>', and '<TMPL_VAR NAME=conditionSetTimeStamp>' in the resource directives. These are not valid values for job submission and must be replaced with concrete values before the script can be run.
issues: The script has a logical flaw in its final status check. It checks for the existence of the error log file and exits with an error code if the file is found. This means the job will be marked as failed simply for producing an error log, even if the error log is empty or contains non-fatal warnings. A better approach would be to check if the error log file is non-empty.
